root_cause.text: The Tegra security engine crypto driver registers asynchronous algorithms without setting the `CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` flag in their `cra_flags` field, which misleads the crypto API into selecting these asynchronous algorithms for synchronous-only requests, resulting in kernel crashes.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that the driver "failed to set the CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC on its asynchronous algorithms, causing the crypto API to select them for users that request only synchronous algorithms. This causes crashes". The patch diff confirms this by adding `CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` to the `.cra_flags` field of various algorithms in `drivers/crypto/tegra/tegra-se-aes.c` and `drivers/crypto/tegra/tegra-se-hash.c`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Tegra Security Engine crypto driver failed to set the `CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` flag in the `cra_flags` field of its asynchronous algorithms.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch diff adds `CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` to the `cra_flags` structure member for multiple algorithms (including `xts(aes)`, `gcm(aes)`, `ccm(aes)`, `cmac(aes)`, and various SHA/HMAC hashes) in `drivers/crypto/tegra/tegra-se-aes.c` and `drivers/crypto/tegra/tegra-se-hash.c` to prevent the crypto API from incorrectly selecting them for synchronous-only requests.

root_cause_review.feedback: The proposed root cause only restates the omission/patch action (failing to set the `CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` flag) without explaining the mechanism of the failure or why this is a problem (i.e., that it causes the crypto API to incorrectly select these asynchronous algorithms for synchronous-only requests, leading to crashes).
